open_points.subject: consumer snapshots and the single home of personal data
open_points.text: “Every other service names a project by the Registry's identity and reads that identity as a snapshot” and “no other service keeps a customer record or a copy of its values, except as fixed in a document it issued” conflict with “Portal serves the last projection it was permitted to keep locally”.
open_points.question: May Client Portal, Cabinet or PresuPro retain snapshots containing living customer or object personal data, and if so, which values and under what explicit exception to R0-80?
options: No service may retain living personal values; snapshots and Portal's offline projection contain only non-personal fields.
Client Portal may retain the personal fields allowed by its token as a specific offline-projection exception.
All trusted consumers may retain the personal fields their contracts allow as snapshots.
open_points.default_guess: Apply the later R0-80 rule: retained consumer snapshots contain no living personal values unless they are fixed in an issued document.

open_points.subject: legacy VPS Registry during migration
open_points.text: “Test instances — any other instance ... Each holds its own identity space and no production personal data” conflicts with the separate “Registry on the VPS” that supplies projects with their customers and objects for production import.
open_points.question: What actor and trust-boundary category does the legacy VPS Registry and its migration export belong to, and is it an explicit temporary exception to the rule that every non-production instance holds no production personal data?
options: A separately named legacy-production migration source that temporarily holds the selected personal data.
A test instance, with the rule changed to allow selected personal data during migration.
Part of the production trust boundary until migration and retirement finish.
open_points.default_guess: Treat it as a separately named legacy-production migration source trusted only for the one controlled export and retired afterward.

open_points.subject: correction of customer kind and fiscal data
open_points.text: “correct a customer ... the Customer with the new contact data” does not say how the newly added `kind`, tax id or legal name can be corrected.
open_points.question: Can the owner correct a customer's kind, tax id and legal name, and if so is that done by `correct a customer` with the same revision and restriction rules?
options: `correct a customer` corrects kind, contact data and fiscal data.
Only contact data is correctable; kind and fiscal data are immutable.
Separate actions correct kind and fiscal data.
open_points.default_guess: Use `correct a customer` for kind, contact data and fiscal data, guarded by the Customer revision.

open_points.subject: billing-data purpose restriction
open_points.text: “a trusted service whose token allows it — today PresuPro, when it issues a document” does not say whether Registry verifies that a document is actually being issued or merely trusts the authenticated service to use the data for that purpose.
open_points.question: What observable input or trust rule makes a billing-data read an allowed document-issuance read, and what failure occurs when that condition is absent?
options: Registry trusts PresuPro's token and the purpose limitation is enforced by PresuPro's contract.
The request supplies a document or issuance reference that Registry validates.
The owner explicitly authorizes each billing-data read.
open_points.default_guess: Registry checks only PresuPro's token; the issuance-purpose limitation is a trusted-service contract outside Registry.

open_points.subject: agent-session access version
open_points.text: “the access version” is returned by `read the session's access`, but no text says which grants, revocations, active-project changes, requests, answers, registrations, archives or erasures advance it, or what the version means.
open_points.question: What state does the access version version, and exactly which accepted actions change it?
options: It versions the entire session-access record, including grants, active project and pending request.
It versions only the granted set and active project.
Separate versions cover access grants and pending requests.
open_points.default_guess: Use one monotonically increasing version for every accepted change to the session's grants, active project or pending request.

open_points.subject: revision checks on owner-interface changes
open_points.text: “Every change ... made against an older revision is refused” applies to the owner interface, while R0-35 gives revisions only to projects and customers after the object revision is removed; owner actions also change session access, artifact pointers, rooms, imports and the audit log.
open_points.question: Which owner-interface changes must carry which revision or version, and what concurrency check applies to changes whose target has no declared revision?
options: Only changes to revision-bearing Project and Customer records carry revisions.
Every mutable aggregate gains a revision or version used by its owner-interface changes.
Non-record actions use action-specific preconditions while Project, Customer and session-access changes use their existing revision or version.
open_points.default_guess: Require Project and Customer revisions and the session access version where applicable; use explicit current-state preconditions for other actions.

open_points.subject: significant audit changes
open_points.text: “Registry records only significant changes of state: changes to projects and customer records, granting and revoking an agent session's projects, restricting processing and lifting it, and erasures and anonymisations.”
open_points.question: Which primary actions are audit-significant, specifically including room and artifact changes, session registration, pending requests and answers, active-project changes, relationship end/resume, imports, failed confirmations and audit-log erasure?
options: The stated categories are exhaustive and all unlisted actions are not audited.
Every successful state-changing primary action is audited.
A separately enumerated subset of the primary actions is audited.
open_points.default_guess: Treat the stated categories as requiring an explicit action-by-action enumeration and audit every successful security-, identity-, retention- or access-relevant state change.

open_points.subject: personal data retained in anonymised artifact pointers
open_points.text: “An anonymised project keeps its id, status and artifact pointers and nothing else” and “It holds no personal value” conflict with R0-68: Registry does not inspect pointer `uri`, `payload_ref` or digest values, and a value that breaks the no-personal-data writer rule is accepted and reaches the agent.
open_points.question: How can anonymisation guarantee that the retained project holds no personal value or permits no re-identification when its uninspected artifact pointers remain?
options: Anonymisation also removes or redacts pointer fields that may identify a person.
The owner must attest before anonymisation that retained pointers contain no identifying values.
The guarantee is weakened: anonymisation removes Registry-classified personal fields but does not guarantee that pointer text is non-personal.
open_points.default_guess: Require the owner's confirmed governance assessment that retained pointers are non-identifying, since Registry cannot inspect them.
